## What changed

Two fixes to the `require-mode` gate shipped in `fork.6`, both found by using
it on a project that already had a `lat.md/` tree.

- **`lat init` now offers the gate to a tree it did not create.** The scaffold
  ran only on the branch that *creates* `lat.md/`, so a re-run picked up the
  instruction block and the conventions skill and silently skipped the flag —
  leaving it unreachable for exactly the projects that needed it. A fresh tree
  is already correct; an existing flat one is the case the rule exists for.

  The offer prints how many documents would need a mode *before* asking,
  because turning the gate on is a decision about how much restructuring to
  take on and cannot be made without the number. Yes stamps the flag and
  creates the missing mode directories. No is recorded in
  `lat.md/.cache/lat_fork.json` and never asked again. A run with no TTY prints
  the frontmatter to paste and records nothing — the shared `ask` returns true
  whenever readline is absent, and a silent yes is the one answer this must not
  give.

- **The flag now merges into frontmatter that already exists.** Answering yes
  did nothing on any root index with a leading `---`: a tree carrying
  `lat: tags: [...]` could never opt in, and `lat init` re-offered every run
  because the flag it thought it had written was not there. Not a duplicate
  block — a silent no-op loop, which is worse.

  A `lat:` mapping now gains `require-mode` as a sibling at whatever
  indentation its existing children use; frontmatter with no `lat:` key gains
  the mapping. The indentation is read from the existing first child rather
  than assumed, because two-space siblings under a four-space mapping is a YAML
  error. `lat: {tags: [x]}` on one line stays refused, and the caller now
  verifies the flag landed and prints the manual edit when it did not, so the
  refusal is visible instead of an offer that repeats forever.

- **Release notes.** Every release now carries them, backfilled to `fork.1`.
  The workflow prefers a tracked file under `.github/release-notes/` and falls
  back to the commit range since the previous tag, so a release is never
  blocked on notes and notes are never a file someone forgot to update.

`INIT_VERSION` is 7, so an existing setup is told to re-run — which is what
surfaces the offer.
